title: The Echo of Kepler Reach
premise: August Fairweather, the last xenolinguist aboard the derelict relay station Kepler Reach, decodes a distress call in Vessic — a language extinct since the colony wars — and discovers two cryo-ships from opposite sides of that war still orbiting the station, each holding half a million sleepers and a claim to the same world. The station's beacon, August learns, was built by their own grandmother to keep both ships asleep forever, an act of vigilante justice meant to starve the war of its armies. When a salvage crew arrives to wake one ship for profit, August must choose between letting history's victors erase the vanquished again or waking both — and trusting enemies to share a future. In the end, August wakes neither: they broadcast the full truth of the war in Vessic and human tongues alike, forcing the salvagers, the colonists' descendants, and the sleeping dead into one negotiated dawn.
about_author: D. M. Ishikawa is the pen name of a former radio astronomer who spent six years calibrating deep-space listening arrays before turning to fiction. They write about languages, machines, and the people paid to stand between them.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: August Fairweather's POV. Establishes daily life on Kepler Reach: maintaining a beacon with no commissioning record, dreaming only in dead languages, rationing loneliness. A routine diagnostic reveals the beacon has been transmitting something extra for years — a pattern August never wrote. Emotional beat: quiet unease beneath ritual calm.

chapters.title: Vessic
chapters.summary: August identifies the hidden transmission as Vessic, extinct since the colony wars ended two centuries ago. Flashbacks to their academy training and their grandmother's unexplained silence about her service era. The signal resolves into grammar — then into a plea. Emotional beat: scholarly thrill curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Two Ships in the Dark
chapters.summary: Following the signal's origin, August's telescope array finds what charts omit: two cryo-ships, Halcyon Dawn and Meridian, locked in a slow gravitational waltz around Kepler Reach. Half a million sleepers each. Emotional beat: vertigo — the station isn't a posting, it's a lock.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Ledger
chapters.summary: In the station archives, August finds handwritten records in their grandmother's hand: she commissioned the beacon. Entries describe 'the long mercy' — keeping both armies asleep until the war's cause died of old age. August realizes they inherited a prison, not a job. Emotional beat: betrayal braided with reluctant admiration.

chapters.title: The Salvage Flag
chapters.summary: Third-person shift to the salvage vessel Coriolis, captained by Rhea Okonkwo, claiming derelict rights over Kepler Reach. Her corporate charter names one prize: a functioning cryo-ship. She detects the Reach's active beacon and alters course. Emotional beat: cold ambition; readers see the threat August cannot.

chapters.title: First Contact Protocol, Improvised
chapters.summary: August's POV. With weeks before the Coriolis arrives, August attempts to answer the Vessic signal and receives structured replies — someone awake aboard Meridian, a single sleeper kept conscious as witness. Her name is Iyo. Emotional beat: first real conversation in years, with a ghost.

chapters.title: What the War Was For
chapters.summary: Iyo's testimony, rendered through August's translation: the war wasn't ideology but water rights, erased from records by the winners aboard Halcyon Dawn. The 'extinct' language was banned, its speakers purged after surrender. Emotional beat: grief for a whole tongue, and anger at tidy histories.

chapters.title: Docking Clamps
chapters.summary: The Coriolis docks. Okonkwo meets August, all charm and contracts, declaring the station salvage and August a squatter with back pay owed. She scans the system and finds the ships within hours. Emotional beat: polite menace; August performs ignorance badly.

chapters.title: Which Half Wakes
chapters.summary: Okonkwo's charter specifies Halcyon Dawn — the victors' ship, whose heirs hold the claims she can sell. August realizes waking it means the purge completes itself in cryo-slow motion. They stall with technical excuses while secretly feeding data to Iyo. Emotional beat: complicity anxiety.

chapters.title: The Witness Wakes
chapters.summary: Iyo asks August to wake her fully — the ship can revive one sleeper safely. Against every protocol, August does. Iyo walks Kepler Reach's corridors, touching her grandmother-language carved into bulkheads by forgotten prisoners. Emotional beat: resurrection as homecoming; the station becomes haunted ground made holy.

chapters.title: Okonkwo's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV shift to Okonkwo. Her own chapter: debt-bonded crew, a corporation that erases failed captains. She knows August is lying and lets them, because a second ship doubles her leverage. Emotional beat: the corrupter revealed as corrupted; power shown as inheritance of another kind.

chapters.title: Grammar of Mutiny
chapters.summary: August teaches Iyo modern Standard while Iyo teaches August Vessic's untranslatable core — words for justice that assume no courts exist. Together they plan to wake Meridian's command crew before Okonkwo can force Halcyon's doors. Emotional beat: conspiracy as intimacy.

chapters.title: Sabotage in Slow Motion
chapters.summary: August falsifies diagnostics to delay the Halcyon breach. Okonkwo's engineer, Sefu, catches the discrepancy but says nothing — his sister sleeps aboard Meridian. First silent ally. Emotional beat: hope arriving disguised as blackmail material.

chapters.title: The Long Mercy Fails
chapters.summary: The beacon's original failsafe — grandmother's final safeguard — triggers when tampering is detected: it begins waking BOTH ships uncontrolled, a cascade no one can stop now. August's sabotage broke the stalemate their grandmother built. Emotional beat: horror at unintended inheritance; the past punishing its heir.

chapters.title: Half a Million Alarm Clocks
chapters.summary: Countdown structure: thaw will complete in nineteen days. Okonkwo moves to seize Halcyon's bridge first; Sefu defects openly; Iyo broadcasts in Vessic across both ships, telling sleepers' future selves what they'll wake to. Emotional beat: accelerating panic, strange solidarity.

chapters.title: Kepler Reach Trial
chapters.summary: Improvised tribunal in the station commons: Okonkwo, August, Iyo, Sefu, and the first revived officers of both ships argue custody of the future. No law covers this. August translates between sides that share no language but blame. Emotional beat: justice outside the law, fragile and improvised.

chapters.title: The World Both Claimed
chapters.summary: Revelation: the contested colony world below has been habitable and empty for two centuries — the war's prize outlasted the war. There is room for everyone, which makes the hatred harder, not easier, to release. Emotional beat: bitter abundance; land as mirror.

chapters.title: Okonkwo's Price
chapters.summary: Okonkwo agrees to arbitration only if her crew's debts are voided and her captaincy recorded honestly — she wants her name cleared of the crime she was going to commit. August brokers it. Emotional beat: corruption negotiating its own redemption at market rate.

chapters.title: Thaw
chapters.summary: Climax. The ships wake fully amid near-mutiny on both sides; hardliners seize Halcyon's armory. Iyo speaks to them in Vessic over open channels — not commands, but the banned mourning songs, sung by a living voice. Weapons lower one by one. Emotional beat: climax as anti-battle; language as disarmament.

chapters.title: Sentences
chapters.summary: Fallout: the tribunal sentences no one to death but assigns everyone labor — rebuilding together, victors and vanquished on the same work crews. August is tried for breaking the beacon and sentenced to teach, which is what they were always doing. Emotional beat: justice as sentence and vocation at once.

chapters.title: Dreaming in Vessic
chapters.summary: Months later. August dreams, for the first time, in a living language — Vessic, now spoken by children born on the voyage down. Grandmother's ledger gets a final entry in August's hand: the long mercy ends. Emotional beat: inheritance transformed; grief composted into continuity.

chapters.title: The Echo of Kepler Reach
chapters.summary: Final chapter, epistolary: August's report to Earth, deliberately delayed so it arrives as history rather than news. The beacon still transmits — now a language lesson, aimed at whoever comes next. Last line: 'We woke everyone. Pray we deserved it.' Emotional beat: earned, uneasy peace; the watch continues.
